html:
The conversion of the First Bulgarian Empire to Christianity, begun when its ruler Boris I was baptised from Constantinople in 864 or 865. The Bulgars, a Turkic people who had settled south of the Danube in 681, ruled a mostly Slavic population, and a shared faith helped unite them.

Boris played Rome and Constantinople against each other, in the years of the Photian schism between them, to win a church of his own. In 870 Bulgaria went with Constantinople and later got its own archbishop. Some nobles rose against the new faith, and Boris put them down harshly.

The turning point came in 886, when disciples of Cyril and Methodius, driven out of Moravia, reached Bulgaria. Boris welcomed them. At schools in Preslav and Ohrid they trained priests who spoke Slavic and translated church books, and the Cyrillic script grew out of their work. Bulgaria became the centre from which Orthodox Christianity and Slavonic letters reached Serbia and the Rus'.
